A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work by Feldman and Shenfeld. The main text, equations, figures and Appendices A–D are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original numerical privacy-accounting results, measured runtimes and simulated mean-estimation errors in Section 5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains original numerical and simulation results and adds Laplace-mechanism evaluations, broader parameter sweeps and nested-sampling comparisons.

M1.justification: The exp-PLD convolution framework remains, but the general-k reduction now mixes floor(t/k) and ceiling(t/k) allocations. Algorithm 1 computes the dual from the original input before discretization, rather than from its discretized approximation. Appendix C also corrects self-convolution control flow and rounding directions. These refine the documented procedure without replacing the approach.

E1.justification: v2 extends evaluation beyond Gaussian mechanisms to Laplace mechanisms and exercises all four combinations of two consecutive Poisson/random-allocation schemes. The Criteo-derived accounting settings, Bernoulli mean-estimation task and PREAMBLE application remain; no new real-data training experiment is reported.

E2.justification: The main Poisson, Feldman–Shenfeld, Dong et al., Monte Carlo and Chua lower-bound comparisons remain. v2 adds comparisons among four nested sampling combinations in Figure 15 and removes the separate comparison against the analytic second-order RDP reference in v1 Figure 9. Newly cited 2026 accounting methods are not added as plotted baselines.

E3.justification: Runtime evaluation changes from runtime versus discretization and step count to runtime versus the computed epsilon-bound gap. The reported FFT comparison changes from sigma=1, delta=10^-6 to sigma=3, delta=10^-10, retaining t=1000. New evaluations specify one versus 100 compositions and additional parameter grids; these do not establish same-setting performance changes.

E4.justification: Appendix D substantially expands sensitivity and applicability analysis through Gaussian parameter-grid comparisons, Laplace/Gaussian comparisons and nested-sampling tests. The second-order RDP diagnostic in v1 Figure 9 is removed, while v2 Figure 14 and Tables 1–2 directly examine how discretization relates to the gap between upper and lower epsilon bounds.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 4 newly reports runtime averages over 10 runs with standard-deviation shading; v1 provides neither that run count nor runtime variability. Both versions retain the Monte Carlo setup of one million importance samples and 95% confidence. The PDFs do not establish an increase in runtime repetitions.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive privacy-bound results for Laplace mechanisms, parameter grids, nested sampling and discretization gaps, while removing the second-order RDP results. Retained results also change: at epsilon=0.1, allocation PLD noise values in the mean-estimation experiment change from 1.89 to 1.88 for d=1 and from 59.68 to 59.56 for d=1000 (v1 Figure 4; v2 Figure 5).

T1.justification: The main theoretical framework remains, with a tighter floor/ceiling reduction and proof in Lemma 2.8. v2 removes the discrete-only restriction on PLD realizations, specifies subsampling support and admissible parameters, and revises the probability-mass interpretation. Appendix B corrects Claim B.2 to use dual infinity masses and repairs endpoint and complexity derivations.

C1.justification: The central claims about efficient PLD accounting and Gaussian privacy–utility advantages remain. Section 1.1 now explicitly restricts the displayed runtime expression to Gaussian mechanisms and includes its sigma dependence; the technical overview also claims the tighter general-k reduction.

C2.justification: v2 explains that the favorable Gaussian comparison does not extend uniformly to Laplace mechanisms: Poisson can be better in higher-privacy regimes. It leaves a general characterization open, qualifies arbitrary-noise applicability by requiring a constructible dominating PLD realization, and explains unresolved comparisons caused by computationally limited bound precision.

D1.justification: Appendix C substantially improves implementation documentation through explicit indexing, endpoint handling, distribution-mixture semantics and disclosure of combined subsampling/re-discretization. Tables 1–2 provide configurations and numerical bounds for the new diagnostic. The code reference changes from RA_PLD to PLD_accounting and adds a package-index link; these are documented access changes, not independently verified availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds Dong and Ganesh (2026), Schuchardt and Kalinin (2026), and Dong and Özgür (2026), positioning the work against newer dynamic-programming accounting and asymptotic sampling analyses. Other changed citation years and venues largely update existing works rather than introduce new research relationships.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar and terminology edits, expands explanations, moves PREAMBLE ahead of runtime and utility discussion, and adds descriptive Appendix D subheadings. Most introductory, methodological and concluding prose retains its original structure.

P2.justification: Figures are broadly redrawn with revised colors, legends, typography and annotations. The runtime display is redesigned, new heatmaps and diagnostic tables are introduced, and several figures are relocated. Appendix C also switches some algorithms to side-by-side layouts. These changes extend well beyond numerical updates or renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves important specification errors in v1, including misplaced self-convolution squaring, reversed convolution rounding and problematic dual construction for lower bounds. Corrected mathematical statements, fuller implementation guidance and direct discretization checks materially strengthen reliability and reproducibility. The Laplace evaluations clarify applicability boundaries. These gains outweigh the loss of the separate second-order RDP diagnostic.
